h: Tying it into a Trotternish loop
p: The Skye Museum of Island Life is a small site, so the best way to enjoy it is as one stop on a bigger loop of the north end of the island. If you're driving clockwise from Portree, you'll follow the east coast past the Old Man of Storr and Kilt Rock before swinging round the top, which puts Kilmuir in your path in the afternoon. Going the other way, it makes a lovely early stop before the drama of the east side.

Just along the coast, the ruins of Duntulm Castle sit on a cliff above the sea, a short walk from the road and a striking spot for photographs on a clear day. Back towards Uig, the Fairy Glen is a strange little landscape of grassy cone-shaped hills and small lochans that children love to clamber about on, and it's become one of the island's favourite short walks.

At the museum itself, take time to read the information in each cottage. There's a lot packed in, from the old ceilidh house to the smithy and the weaver's cottage, and the details tell you how hard people worked just to stay warm and fed. Being on an exposed hilltop, it can be blowy, so hats and windproof jackets are your friends.

Food and fuel can be few and far between up here, so fill up in Portree or Uig and bring snacks for the car. Portree's colourful harbour is the perfect place to finish the day, with places to eat looking out over the boats.
